item.title: This lawyer believes in second chances. Now AI is providing a boost
item.description: Tens of millions of Americans have criminal records that can be barriers to employment. An AI-powered app is helping those eligible to expunge their records at a pace not seen before.

item.title: Rare photos of ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi give her family hope
item.description: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, told NPR that photographs of his mother meeting a foreign official gave him "a reason to hope" for the first time since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Over 4 million people are no longer receiving food aid amid sweeping changes to SNAP
item.description: SNAP, also known as food stamps, has seen a rapid and consistent participation decline since last July. The drop comes as the program faces historic cuts and changes.

item.title: The DOJ is increasingly charging ICE protesters with criminal conspiracy
item.description: The Justice Department is using federal conspiracy charges to sweep up ICE protesters. Some legal experts worry the agency is casting too wide a net to prosecute political activists who oppose the Trump administration's deportation agenda.

item.title: For Republicans planning post-Trump future, one race in Washington is worth watching
item.description: The primary to replace Rep. Dan Newhouse is a rare opportunity for Washington's Republicans to seek federal office. Candidates representing different wings of the party are testing Trump's influence.

item.title: Israel says it has serious concerns with Hamas disarmament deal
item.description: President Trump announced a proposed disarmament deal with Hamas last week. Israeli strikes overnight and into Sunday evening killed at least 17 people, including children, in Gaza.

item.title: South Korea ditches 'denuclearization-first' strategy. What will Pyongyang do next?
item.description: South Korea is moving away from its policy of prioritizing the immediate denuclearization of North Korea. But despite that shift, experts doubt Pyongyang will return to the negotiating table.

item.title: U.S. dollar weakens sharply against the Japanese yen after market interventions
item.description: The U.S. dollar weakened sharply Monday against the Japanese yen after U.S. President Donald Trump and Japan's finance minister confirmed both sides had intervened in markets.

item.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche issued a formal order late Sunday terminating President Donald Trump's $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization fund" to compensate his political allies.
